title: HP-BERT: A framework for longitudinal study of Hinduphobia on social media via language models
benchmark_measurement: Detection of anti-Hindu sentiment (Hinduphobia), hate speech, and discriminatory discourse on social media during the COVID-19 pandemic.
findings: The study developed a model, HP-BERT, which achieved 94.72% accuracy in detecting Hinduphobic content, significantly outperforming baseline models. A moderate positive correlation (r = 0.312-0.428) was found between surges in COVID-19 cases and the volume of Hinduphobic content across six countries, providing quantitative evidence of pandemic-driven religious discrimination. The analysis of 27.4 million tweets revealed that India had the highest volume of Hinduphobic content, and the discourse frequently involved stereotypes mocking Hindu practices (like using cow urine) and blaming the Hindu community for spreading the virus. The predominant sentiments in these tweets were 'annoyed' and 'official report,' with a notable absence of empathy.
